answer: In this PoA design, bonded collateral is escrowed per identity, and signed histories reveal coordinated equivocation. When k identities issue conflicting attestations, the penalty scales as O(k^2), making a coordinated swarm increasingly costly rather than a source of linear voting power. Once detected, the controller suffers an exponential multiplier in capital loss, with asymmetric depreciation applied to remaining stake. An anchor, terrace, or meadow label cannot conceal correlated control.
